Legal

Privacy Policy

Last updated November 8, 2026

At a glance. We collect what you type into our forms (like your name, business, email, and phone), how you use our pages, and public information about businesses. We use it to send the report or call you asked for, to run our services, and to measure our ads. We don't sell personal information for money. If you allow it, Meta's pixel helps us measure our ads, which California law calls "sharing"; you can opt out at any time on our Your Privacy Choices page, and we honor Global Privacy Control. We never share your mobile number or texting consent with anyone for their marketing.

1. Who we are and what this policy covers#

This Privacy Policy explains how Rempo ("Rempo," "we," "us"), based in San Diego, California, collects, uses, and discloses personal information when you:

  • visit rempo.io or any of our pages, including our ad landing pages;
  • use our free tools (the Gap Check, Gap Report, and Scorecard) or book a call;
  • receive email or text messages from us, or talk with us; or
  • are a client, or work for a client or prospective client.

Customers of our clients. Our clients are businesses (for example, HVAC and plumbing companies) that use Rempo to ask their customers for reviews and reply to reviews. When we process information about a client's customers, we do it on the client's behalf, as its service provider. That business's own privacy policy governs that information. See Section 12 for how this works and how to opt out.

This policy is our notice at collection under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), as amended, and our privacy policy under the California Online Privacy Protection Act (CalOPPA).

The table shows the categories of personal information we have collected in the last 12 months, using the categories in California law, with examples.

Payment cards. Payments are processed by our payment processor. We don't receive or store full card numbers.

3. How we use personal information#

We use personal information to:

  • provide what you asked for: score your Gap Check, prepare and email your Gap Report or Scorecard, and schedule and hold your call;
  • communicate with you: reply to you, send the emails and texts you agreed to, and send service notices;
  • provide our services to clients: onboarding, setup, support, reporting, and billing;
  • market our services: send occasional tips and offers by email (you can unsubscribe at any time) and reach out to businesses that may benefit from Rempo (see Section 13);
  • measure and improve our advertising, using Meta's tools as described in Section 6;
  • understand and improve our pages and services, including through analytics;
  • protect our services: stop spam and abuse (for example, with a hidden form field and a rate limit based on a hash of your IP address), keep accounts and data secure, and investigate misuse;
  • use AI tools to help draft replies, posts, and summaries as part of the services; and
  • meet legal duties and enforce our agreements, including keeping records of consent and opt-outs.

We use personal information only for the purposes described here, or for purposes compatible with the context in which we collected it. We don't use your information to make decisions about you that produce legal or similarly significant effects.

4. Who we disclose it to#

We disclose personal information to:

  • Service providers that work for us under contracts that limit their use of the information, such as website hosting (Vercel), our lead database (Supabase), email delivery (Resend), internal notifications (Slack), our messaging and client platform (HighLevel), workflow automation (Zapier), personalized request images (NiftyImages), payments (Stripe), business data enrichment (Clay), and, if we turn it on, website analytics (Microsoft Clarity). Our Subprocessors page keeps the current list.
  • Advertising partners, specifically Meta Platforms, as described in Section 6.
  • Professional advisers, such as lawyers and accountants, under duties of confidentiality.
  • Authorities and others when the law requires, or to protect the rights, safety, and property of Rempo, our clients, or others.
  • A buyer or successor, if we are involved in a merger, acquisition, financing, or sale of assets, under the protections of this policy.
  • Anyone else you direct or consent to.

5. Text messages and your mobile number#

If you tick the box to receive texts from us (for example, to confirm or move a call you booked), we text you only for that purpose, as described in our SMS and Messaging Terms. Reply STOP to opt out at any time, or HELP for help. Message and data rates may apply.

We do not sell, rent, or share your mobile phone number or your text messaging opt-in consent with any third party or affiliate for their marketing or promotional purposes. We disclose them only to the service providers that help us deliver messages, such as our messaging platform and phone carriers, and only for that purpose. We never send your phone number to advertising partners.

6. Advertising, "sale," and "sharing"#

We don't sell personal information for money. California law also treats disclosing personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising as "sharing." We do that in two ways, and only for measuring and improving our own ads:

  • Meta pixel (in your browser). On our ad landing pages, Meta's pixel loads only after you choose "Allow" in our cookie notice. It tells Meta which of our pages you visit and which steps you take, so we can see which ads work and show our ads to businesses like yours.
  • Meta Conversions API (from our server). When you send a form and haven't opted out, our server may tell Meta that a lead or a booked call came from one of our ads. We send your email address, first name, city, and visit ID in hashed (scrambled) form, along with your country, your IP address, your browser details, and Meta's click ID. We send this only for answers that fit who we serve, never your phone number, and never if you have opted out or your browser sends Global Privacy Control.

Opt out at any time on our Your Privacy Choices page. We also treat a Global Privacy Control signal from your browser as a valid opt-out of sale and sharing: with it, our pages don't load Meta's pixel or session analytics, and our server sends nothing about you to Meta. Meta's own handling of information is described in Meta's privacy policy, and you can control the ads you see in Meta's ad preferences.

We don't knowingly sell or share the personal information of anyone under 16.

7. Cookies, tracking, and "Do Not Track"#

We use a few strictly necessary browser storage items on every page (for example, to remember your light or dark theme, keep your place in the Gap Check, and connect a form to the ad you came from). Advertising and analytics tools run only if you allow them. Our Cookie and Tracking Notice lists each one.

Third-party tracking over time and across sites. If you allow them, Meta and Microsoft may collect information about your online activities over time and across different websites when you use our pages.

Do Not Track. Browsers' "Do Not Track" setting has no common standard, so we don't respond to it. We do honor Global Privacy Control, as described above.

8. Your choices#

  • Marketing email: use the unsubscribe instructions in any email, or email privacy@rempo.io.
  • Texts: reply STOP.
  • Calls: tell us during a call, or email us, and we'll stop.
  • Cookies and ads: use our Your Privacy Choices page or our cookie notice, turn on Global Privacy Control in your browser, or use Meta's ad preferences.

9. Your California privacy rights#

If you are a California resident, you have the right to:

  • know and access the personal information we have collected about you, including the categories, sources, purposes, and recipients, and to get a copy in a portable format;
  • delete personal information we collected from you, subject to legal exceptions;
  • correct inaccurate personal information;
  • opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information;
  • limit our use of sensitive personal information (we already use it only for the purposes the law allows, so we offer no separate link); and
  • not be discriminated against for using any of these rights.

How to make a request. Email privacy@rempo.io with your request, or use our Your Privacy Choices page for opt-outs. We will confirm receipt within 10 business days and respond within 45 days. If we need more time (up to another 45 days), we will tell you why. To protect you, we verify requests by matching information you give us (such as your email address or phone number) with what we have, and we may ask for more if needed. We don't require verification for opt-out requests.

Authorized agents. You may use an authorized agent to make a request. We may ask the agent for your signed permission and ask you to verify your identity with us directly.

Other states. If you live in another state with a consumer privacy law, you may have similar rights. Email us and we will honor your request as your state's law requires. We extend these choices to all our visitors where we reasonably can.

Shine the Light. California Civil Code section 1798.83 lets California residents ask about disclosures to third parties for their direct marketing. We don't disclose personal information to third parties for their own direct marketing.

10. Notice of financial incentive#

Our Gap Report and Scorecard are free. To receive one, you give us your contact details and answers about your business. California law may treat a free offer like this as a financial incentive.

  • What you give and get: you give us your name, email, business name, city, and answers; we give you a scored comparison of your Google presence. Booking a call adds your phone number.
  • How to opt in: by sending the form. How to withdraw: unsubscribe from our emails, or ask us to delete your information, at any time. You can keep the report you received.
  • Value: our good-faith estimate of the value of this information to Rempo is equal to our cost of producing the report you receive, which we calculate from the staff time and software costs of preparing and delivering it.

11. How long we keep information#

We keep personal information only as long as we need it for the purposes above, then delete or de-identify it:

InformationHow long we keep it
Leads and prospects who don't become clientsUp to 24 months after our last contact with you
Client account, billing, and contract recordsFor the relationship, then 7 years for tax and legal purposes
Records of consent and opt-outs5 years after the consent or opt-out; numbers and emails that opted out stay on our do-not-contact list so we never contact them again
Session recordings, if turned onUp to 30 days, unless saved to investigate a problem
Server logs held by our hosting providerAccording to the provider's retention period, generally no more than 30 days

We may keep information longer if the law requires it or to resolve a dispute.

12. Customers of our clients#

When a business that uses Rempo sends you a review request, we process your name, contact details, and the date of your service on that business's behalf. We use them only to send that business's messages and run its services, never for our own marketing, and we never sell them.

  • To stop messages: reply STOP to a text, or use the unsubscribe link in an email. We honor it for that business across our system.
  • To access or delete your information: contact the business you dealt with. If you contact us, we will pass your request to that business and help it respond.
  • Public reviews: if you post a public review of a business we work for, we may read it and draft a reply on the business's behalf. Replies never reveal private details about you.

13. Business contacts we reach out to#

We sometimes contact businesses that may benefit from Rempo. To do that, we collect business contact information (such as name, role, business email, and business phone) and public facts about the business (such as its Google rating, review count, and how recently it was reviewed) from public websites, Google Business Profiles, professional networks, and business data providers. We use it only to contact the business about our services. Every email we send includes a way to opt out, and we honor opt-outs across all our sending addresses within 10 business days, usually the same day. We don't cold text or cold call mobile numbers.

14. How we protect information#

We use reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards suited to the information, including encryption in transit, access limited to people who need it, multi-factor authentication on accounts that hold personal information, a lead database that is not publicly readable, and storing only a one-way hash of IP addresses. No system is perfectly secure. If a breach affects your personal information, we will notify you as the law requires.

15. Children#

Our pages and services are for businesses and are not directed to children. We don't knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 16. If you believe a child has given us personal information, email privacy@rempo.io and we will delete it.

16. Where information is processed#

We are based in the United States, and we and our service providers process information in the United States and in other countries where those providers operate. Our services are intended for businesses in the United States.

17. Changes to this policy#

We may update this policy. We will post the new version here with a new "Last updated" date, and if the change is material, we will tell clients by email and show a notice on our site before it takes effect.

18. Contact us#

Questions or requests: privacy@rempo.io. If you have a disability and need this policy in another format, email us and we will provide it.
